survey: A stage spotlight hanging from a truss, seen from below and to the left. The truss is a flat two-chord truss: two parallel tubes joined by zig-zag diagonal tubes, with rounded end caps. Two clamps with orange bolts wrap the lower tube, one on the left and one on the right. A rigid U-shaped yoke runs down from the bar joining the two clamps. The yoke wraps around the light and meets the sides of the can at two pivot points, each with an orange tightening knob: one is visible on the right side, and a small one shows on the far left side. That is how a real tilting yoke works. The can is a closed cylinder with vent slots on top and a front rim and lens face. Three round LED lenses (yellow, cyan and red) sit inside the rim and face the camera toward the lower left. Coloured beams leave the lenses in the direction the can points. There is no power cable; that is a normal simplification, not an error.
